chunks: And it is narrated from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar al-Juʿfī, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying:
Regarding the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “But no! I swear by the setting places of the stars. And indeed it is surely a tremendous oath, if you but knew.”
By it, he means the oath of disassociation from the Imams عليهم السلام, by which a man swears.
He says: indeed that is tremendous in the sight of Allah.

key_terms.عَظِيمٌ: tremendous, immense in gravity and seriousness
key_terms.مَوَاقِعِ ٱلنُّجُومِ: the setting places or positions of the stars, cited here from the Qur'anic oath

ai.seo_question: What does the verse about the setting of the stars mean in relation to disassociation from the Imams?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام explains this Qur'anic oath as referring to the grave matter of swearing disassociation from the Imams عليهم السلام. The narration presents such an oath as immensely serious before Allah, highlighting the sanctity of allegiance to the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4326 - Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar al-Ju'fi narrated that he heard

regarding the words of Allah (swt), the Almighty and Glorious:
"But no! I swear by the setting of the stars. And indeed, it is a mighty oath-if you only knew" (Surah Al-Waqi'ah 56:75-76).
Imam (as) said: "It refers to the oath of disassociation from the Imams (peace be upon them), where a man swears by it.
Verily, such an oath is considered great in the sight of Allah (swt)."
